about: Where scripts/update-events.mjs looks for new or changed event information, and how to check each place. Organizer pages are the most authoritative source for dates and venues; Wizards' announcements are authoritative for which events exist. Kinds: 'magicgg-news' and 'wizards-news' are article lists (each new matching article is read once), 'rss' is a feed (same), 'page' is one page read again whenever its text changes. 'match' and 'exclude' are case-insensitive regexes tested against an article's title, URL and categories.

sources.name: magic.gg news
sources.check: Wizards' competitive news site. Announces Spotlight stops, Regional Championship rounds ("Play Update" posts), Pro Tour and Worlds fact sheets, and posts final standings, decklists and metagame breakdowns after each event. Use it for new events, invitations and prizes, and for results, decklists and coverage links on events already listed.

sources.name: Wizards of the Coast announcements
sources.check: Season-level announcements: the yearly competitive calendar, MagicCon locations, new event series and format changes. The list gives no dates, so each matching announcement is read once.

sources.name: Star City Games articles
sources.check: SCG's news feed, with full article text. SCG hosts the US Regional Championships and US Spotlight stops at SCG CON, and often reports schedule and promo news before magic.gg does. Only Magic articles about competitive events matter.
sources.exclude: riftbound|lorcana|flesh and blood|pok[eé]mon|sorcery|star wars|commander vs|spike feeders

sources.name: SCG CON schedule
sources.check: The organizer's own list of every upcoming SCG CON: city, convention dates and venue, with a link per show (scgcon.starcitygames.com/event/...). An SCG CON runs Friday to Sunday; the premier event inside it may run all three days or only two. Use it to confirm dates and venues of US Regional Championships and US Spotlight stops (venue as "SCG CON <City>, <Convention center>", links.event as the show's page). A show that hosts no event we list is not an event to add.

sources.name: Fanfinity upcoming events
sources.check: Fanfinity's own list of its upcoming Magic events in Europe: Spotlight stops, Ultimate Guard European Magic Series Regional Championships, and CommandFest weekends held alongside the Spotlights. Use it to confirm dates and cities of European Spotlights and RCs, and to add any it lists that we don't. CommandFest and side events are not events we list.

sources.name: Fanfinity news
sources.check: Fanfinity's blog: event announcements, venue and schedule details, and recaps for its European Spotlights and Regional Championships (the Ultimate Guard European Magic Series).

sources.name: F2F Tour destination events
sources.check: Face to Face Games' list of its Canadian Tour Weekends, which host the Canadian Regional Championships and Spotlight stops. Use it for their dates, cities and venues.

sources.name: F2F Tour news
sources.check: F2F Tour news: announcements and details for Canadian Regional Championships, Spotlight stops and Tour Weekends. Store qualifiers (RCQs, last-chance qualifiers) are not events we list.

sources.name: Central America Magic Series
sources.check: The site of Necrotower's Central America Magic Series, which runs the Mexico, Central America and Caribbean Regional Championships (in Mexico City). Use it to confirm their dates and venue. In Spanish.

organizers.name: Star City Games
organizers.hosts: US Regional Championships and US Spotlight stops (at SCG CON)
organizers.check: SCG CON schedule (source 'scgcon'); event pages at https://scgcon.starcitygames.com/event/<show>/

organizers.name: Fanfinity
organizers.hosts: Europe, Middle East and Africa Regional Championships and European Spotlight stops
organizers.check: Watched: its upcoming-events page and news feed (sources 'fanfinity-events', 'fanfinity-news'). Site: https://www.fanfinity.gg

organizers.name: Face to Face Games
organizers.hosts: Canadian Regional Championships and Canadian Spotlight stops (at F2F Tour weekends)
organizers.check: Watched: the F2F Tour destination-events page and news feed (sources 'f2f-destination', 'f2f-news'). Its events iCal feed (https://f2ftour.com/events/?ical=1) is mostly store qualifiers, so it isn't watched.

organizers.name: BIG MAGIC
organizers.hosts: Japanese Regional Championships and Japanese Spotlight stops
organizers.check: Not watched yet: the Champions Cup pages (Japan's Regional Championship series, https://ssl.bigmagic.net/championscup/) are drawn by JavaScript, so a plain fetch gets no text, and https://mtg.bigmagic.net is mostly shop and strategy articles. Japanese RCs and Spotlights come in through magic.gg.

organizers.name: Let's Play Games
organizers.hosts: Australia and New Zealand Regional Championships and Spotlight stops
organizers.check: Not watched: its site blocks automated visitors. ANZ RCs and Spotlights come in through magic.gg.

organizers.name: Kadou
organizers.hosts: Regional Championships and Spotlight stops in mainland China
organizers.check: Not watched: no official schedule page found (as of 2026-11-22). China's RC (the MTG China Open) comes in through magic.gg.

organizers.name: Necrotower
organizers.hosts: Mexico, Central America and Caribbean Regional Championships
organizers.check: Watched: the Central America Magic Series site (source 'cams').

organizers.name: Devir Brasil
organizers.check: Not watched: no current schedule page. https://southamericamagicseries.com belongs to the previous organizer (Magicsur) and hasn't been updated since June 2025. South American RCs come in through magic.gg.

organizers.name: Game Square
organizers.check: Not watched: no official schedule page found (as of 2026-11-22). Chinese Taipei's RC comes in through magic.gg.

organizers.name: Oracle Events
organizers.check: Not watched: no official schedule page found (as of 2026-11-22). Southeast Asia's RC (the SEA Championship) comes in through magic.gg.
